memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You shall speak to him and put words in his mouth; I will help both of you speak and will teach you what to do. He will speak to the people for you, and it will be as though he were your mouth and as though you were God to him. But take this staff in your hand so that you can perform the signs with it." - Exodus 4:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God works out the arrangement in detail. Moses will receive the word, Aaron will speak it, and God will help them both. The plan now involves two brothers rather than one man.

This is a picture of how God usually works. He rarely gives one person every gift. He builds teams. He puts the thinker beside the speaker, the organiser beside the visionary, the quiet servant beside the public leader.

Paul describes exactly this — one body, many parts, none able to say to another, I do not need you (1 Cor 12:21). Your church needs the person whose gifts are nothing like yours.

That has two implications. First, stop resenting what you lack; God has probably placed someone nearby who supplies it. Second, stop hiding what you have; someone nearby is lacking it.

And notice the last line — take this staff. The ordinary shepherd's stick is now called the instrument of God's signs. What Moses surrendered has been fully commissioned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who has God placed beside me to supply what I lack?
2. What gift am I withholding that someone else needs?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I do not have to be everything. Help me to serve gladly alongside others and to value what they bring. Amen.
